key_insight: Accurate tumor-growth curve fits and plausible AI explanations can mask incorrect governing growth laws.
clinical_relevance: This modeling study supports more rigorous validation of AI-assisted tumor-growth models but does not establish clinical utility or drug-discovery benefits.
method: Generate candidate growth laws using symbolic regression and check mathematical admissibility.
Refit coefficients using physics-informed neural networks or nonlinear least squares.
Explore archived LLM rankings against selection by training error.
evidence_signal: Synthetic Gompertz experiments recovered the generating family with dense noiseless data, but sparse noisy data often yielded alternative laws; nonlinear least squares usually reduced law error, while neural-network refitting often increased it.
watch_item: Synthetic-data results and exploratory LLM rankings do not establish reliability in patient data; forecasting accuracy and growth-law recovery require separate evaluation.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
